stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 40%, and then the new price is decreased by 9%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 40% increase: $100 \times (1 + 40/100) = 140.00$. After a 9% decrease on 140.00: $140.00 \times (1 - 9/100) = 127.40$. Net change $= 127.40 - 100 = 27.40\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 40 - 9 - \dfrac{360}{100} = 27.40\%$.
